workload.description: 50k ID/s; Snowflake-style in-process generation with a DB segment allocator for monotonic ranges

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 50,000 IDs/s peak. 97% single-ID generation, 2% bulk block reservation, 1% decode/lookup of an existing ID.

assumptions.subject: app
assumptions.statement: ID generation is pure in-process arithmetic (no network hop on the hot path), so an ID node is CPU/network bound at ~6,000 rps on a 2-vCPU c7g.large.

assumptions.subject: coord
assumptions.statement: Worker-ID lease is checked at startup and heartbeated, not per request; modelled as a 5% visit on the generate path. etcd is modelled with the `cache` kind - Keystone v1 has no dedicated coordination-store kind, and a KV store is the closest honest shape.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The Postgres segment allocator is touched once per 1,000 IDs on the hot path (visit_prob 0.001) because each node buffers a block locally. A single primary at ~8,000 rps is sufficient by two orders of magnitude - it is sized for durability and HA, not throughput.

assumptions.subject: clock
assumptions.statement: Snowflake correctness depends on monotonic wall-clock time. Clock skew / leap-second stalls are a CORRECTNESS failure mode, not a capacity one, and the v1 analytical engine cannot model them - it computes throughput and latency only. Treat NTP discipline and the reject-on-backwards-clock guard as an unmodelled requirement.

_library.summary: Snowflake-style service that hands out globally unique, roughly time-ordered 64-bit IDs at high rate.
